correctness.rationale: The action is free since every nontrivial row rotation changes the uniquely occupied row in each occupied column. There are two edge types on each column pair and two triangle types on each triple; oriented row differences give the two recorded boundary words. Collapsing the spanning tree makes the two relators on 0,i,j solve for e⁺ij=xj and e⁻ij=xi⁻¹. The remaining words are xj xk xi and xi⁻¹ xj⁻¹ xk⁻¹. Successive positive triangle relators 123, 124, 134 solve for x1=x3⁻¹x2⁻¹, x4=x3, x2=x3, and 12t solves for xt=x3 at every t≥5. Each solved letter occurs once and is absent from the solving word. Such a one/two-cell move preserves the complex up to homotopy: homotope all other attaching loops in the subcomplex containing the solving cell to replace the eliminated letter by its path there, then collapse that cell with its single remaining edge occurrence. Thus x1=x⁻² and all others=x. Words involving 1 then have exponent 0; all others have exponent ±3, with 234 available already at n=5. Attach one degree-three cell; all other loops are now null and attaching along them wedges on 2-spheres. The count 2·binom(n−1,3)−(n−2)−1 is the asserted β. The frozen finite checker was read, not executed; the word argument works for all widths without extrapolation.

evidence: Dyer–Sieradski classify every connected finite 2-complex with fundamental group Z/m as Pm wedged with rank H2 copies of S². The primary 1973 Bulletin PDF's indexed statement was corroborated by full OA reading of Lemmas 5.4 and 5.7 of The Capacity of Some Classes of Polyhedra, which attributes the wedge lemma to their 1973 Commentarii paper.
